title: Appeal of RE Charles Kim v. Korean Capital Presbytery
disposition_detail: Issue: Whether Korean Capital Presbytery or its January 8, 2001 Special Judicial Commission was the proper court to assume original jurisdiction over charges against the appellant. Held: No; original jurisdiction lay with the Session. The Presbytery's and Commission's actions in the matter were reversed. The reversal did not adjudicate the merits of the schism and contumacy charges.
first_summary: On appeal from an excommunication, the SJC reversed because Korean Capital Presbytery and its special judicial commission were not the proper court of original jurisdiction over charges against a communicant member. Original jurisdiction belonged to the local Session. The SJC reversed the excommunication.
summary: On appeal from an excommunication, the SJC held that Korean Capital Presbytery and its special judicial commission were not the proper court of original jurisdiction to adjudicate charges against a communicant member. Because original jurisdiction belonged to the local session, the Presbytery/commission proceedings against the member were unconstitutional and reversed. The ruling turned only on jurisdiction; it did not decide the truth of the schism and contumacy charges. The excommunication therefore could not stand on that record.
